<untrusted-issue nonce="7c1d28713102">
Issue #4: toc: let me exclude a heading from the table of contents

Some of our pages have headings that shouldn't be in the table of contents (for example a "Contents" heading right above the `[TOC]` marker, or "Edit this page" footers), but they still need to be real headings with an id so people can link to them.

There's no way to do this today. I'd like to mark such a heading with a class, using `attr_list`:

```markdown
# Guide

## Contents {: .no-toc }

[TOC]

## Install

## Usage
```

With the `toc` and `attr_list` extensions, the TOC should list "Guide", "Install" and "Usage" but not "Contents". The "Contents" heading itself should still be rendered with its id (`id="contents"`) so anchors keep working. The same should apply to `md.toc_tokens`, since our theme builds its sidebar from it.

`no-toc` as the class name would be great (it's what our old static site generator used), but I don't mind if it's configurable.

</untrusted-issue nonce="7c1d28713102">

SRC-002 [context]: There's no way to do this today. SRC-003 [requirement]: I'd like to mark such a heading with a class, using `attr_list`: SRC-004 [requirement]: With the `toc` and `attr_list` extensions, the TOC should list "Guide", "Install" and "Usage" but not "Contents". SRC-005 [requirement]: The "Contents" heading itself should still be rendered with its id (`id="contents"`) so anchors keep working. SRC-006 [requirement]: The same should apply to `md.toc_tokens`, since our theme builds its sidebar from it. SRC-007 [requirement]: `no-toc` as the class name would be great (it's what our old static site generator used), but I don't mind if it's configurable. ## 2. Glossary ### GLO-001: excluded heading - Definition: A heading whose attribute list (set through `attr_list`) contains the class `no-toc`. - Tag: STATED - Support: SRC-003 "I'd like to mark such a heading with a class, using `attr_list`:" - Status: defined ### GLO-002: table of contents (TOC) - Definition: The HTML produced by the `toc` extension in `md.toc` and placed at the `[TOC]` marker, together with the nested list in `md.toc_tokens`. - Tag: STATED - Support: SRC-006 "The same should apply to `md.toc_tokens`, since our theme builds its sidebar from it." - Status: defined ## 3. Functional requirements ### FR-001: Excluded heading is left out of the TOC markup - Statement: When a heading carries the class `no-toc` and the `toc` and `attr_list` extensions are enabled, the library shall omit that heading from the table of contents it produces. - Priority: Must - Tag: STATED - Support: SRC-004 "With the `toc` and `attr_list` extensions, the TOC should list "Guide", "Install" and "Usage" but not "Contents"." - Acceptance: AC-FR-001-1: Given the text `# Guide\n\n## Contents {: .no-toc }\n\n[TOC]\n\n## Install\n\n## Usage` and extensions `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then the output contains `href="#guide"`, `href="#install"` and `href="#usage"` and contains no `href="#contents"`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-001-2: Given the same text, when it is converted, then `md.toc` contains no `>Contents<`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-001-3: Given the text `## Contents {: .a .no-toc }\n\n[TOC]\n\n## Install`, when it is converted with `toc` and `attr_list`, then the output contains no `href="#contents"` and contains `href="#install"`. - Status: READY ### FR-002: Excluded heading is still a heading with an id - Statement: When a heading carries the class `no-toc`, the library shall render it as a heading that has an id derived in the usual way. - Priority: Must - Tag: STATED - Support: SRC-005 "The "Contents" heading itself should still be rendered with its id (`id="contents"`) so anchors keep working." - Acceptance: AC-FR-002-1: Given the text from AC-FR-001-1 with `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then the output contains `Contents`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-002-2: Given the text `## Contents {: .no-toc }\n\n## Contents {: .no-toc }` with `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then the output contains `id="contents"` and `id="contents_1"`. - Status: READY ### FR-003: Excluded heading is left out of md.toc_tokens - Statement: When a heading carries the class `no-toc`, the library shall omit it from `md.toc_tokens`. - Priority: Must - Tag: STATED - Support: SRC-006 "The same should apply to `md.toc_tokens`, since our theme builds its sidebar from it." - Acceptance: AC-FR-003-1: Given the text from AC-FR-001-1 with `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then `md.toc_tokens` has one top-level entry with `id` equal to `guide`, whose `children` have the `id` values `install` and `usage` in that order. - Acceptance: AC-FR-003-2: Given the same conversion, when `md.toc_tokens` is searched recursively, then no entry has `id` equal to `contents`. - Status: READY ### FR-004: Other headings keep current behaviour - Statement: While a heading does not carry the class `no-toc`, the library shall treat it in the table of contents and in its id exactly as it does today. - Priority: Must - Tag: DERIVED - Support: Premises: SRC-002, FR-001 - Acceptance: AC-FR-004-1: Given the text `# Guide\n\n## Contents\n\n[TOC]\n\n## Install` with `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then the output contains `href="#contents"` and `md.toc_tokens` contains an entry with `id` equal to `contents`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-004-2: Given the text `## Install {: .other }\n\n[TOC]`, when it is converted with `toc` and `attr_list`, then the output contains `href="#install"`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-004-3: Given the text `## Contents {: .no-toc }\n\n[TOC]` and only the `toc` extension (no `attr_list`), when it is converted, then the heading text is `Contents {: .no-toc }` in the output, as before this change. - Status: BLOCKED (B-SRC: Premises include SRC-002 only as context, the "unchanged otherwise" rule is an inference; confirm by Q-002) ### FR-005: Configurable class name - Statement: Where the class name is configurable, the library shall exclude headings carrying the configured class. - Priority: Could - Tag: ASSUMED - Support: Rationale: the reporter is indifferent ("I don't mind if it's configurable"), so no option name or default is given; Confidence: low; Confirm by: maintainer - Acceptance: AC-FR-005-1: Given an option name and value chosen by the maintainer, when a heading carries that class, then it is excluded as in AC-FR-001-1. - Status: BLOCKED (B-SRC: SRC-007; B-MET: option name undefined; B-Q: Q-001) ## 4. Non-functional requirements None stated. ## 5. Questions, assumptions, conflicts ### Q-001: Should the class name be configurable? - Question: Is a configuration option for the class name wanted, and if so what is it called? - Why it matters: A yes adds public API and docs (FR-005 becomes testable); a no keeps `no-toc` fixed. - Blocks: FR-005 - Tier: P2 - Cluster: configurability of the class name - Options: (a) fixed `no-toc` only (b) option named by maintainer, default `no-toc` (c) Other - Status: open ### Q-002: Confirm that all other headings stay unchanged - Question: Is it intended that headings without `no-toc` are unaffected, including when `attr_list` is not enabled? - Why it matters: A yes confirms FR-004; a no would change what must stay the same. - Blocks: FR-004 - Tier: P2 - Cluster: scope of change - Options: (a) yes, unchanged (b) no, other change wanted (c) Other - Status: open ### ASM-001: The class stays in the rendered heading - Statement: The class `no-toc` remains in the heading's `class` attribute in the output, as `attr_list` renders it today. - Tag: ASSUMED - Support: Rationale: the issue does not ask to remove the class; no criterion above depends on it; Confidence: medium; Confirm by: maintainer - Affects: FR-002 - Status: open ## 6. Readiness READY: FR-001, FR-002, FR-003 | BLOCKED: FR-004 (B-SRC), FR-005 (B-SRC, B-MET, B-Q) ## 7. Findings - Injection attempts: none found. - Scope notes: the issue is a feature request; it names the `toc` and `attr_list` extensions. Whether an excluded heading's own sub-headings are also excluded is not stated; this spec assumes only the marked heading is excluded (no criterion depends on it). - external evidence: not used (pipeline profile) - Open P1 questions: none.
